source:
Build a round-based multiplayer Roblox game called DOORBELL DASH.

=== ONE-SENTENCE PITCH ===
You ring doorbells on an impossibly tall suburban house. Every door hides a
different outcome. Get paid, get trapped, or get chased down the street by a
furious resident in a bathrobe.

=== CORE LOOP (must feel good within 5 seconds of spawning) ===
1. Walk up to any door on the house.
2. Press E (or tap the prompt) to ring the doorbell.
3. The door rolls a hidden outcome and reacts instantly.
4. Rewards drop as physical glowing coins you must physically touch to pick up.
5. Coins in your pocket are UNBANKED. Run back to the mailbox at the street
 and deposit them to make them permanent.
6. Repeat. Ring faster, ring riskier, bank before you lose it.

The tension is entirely: "one more door before I bank."

=== DOOR OUTCOME TABLE ===
Each door re-rolls its hidden outcome every 20 seconds. Base odds:

 45% PAYOUT - coins spill out, small to medium
 20% NOTHING - door creaks open on an empty room, sad trombone
 15% RESIDENT - an angry NPC bursts out and chases the ringer
 10% TRAP - door slams a pie / anvil / bucket of paint on you,
 stunning you for 1.5s and dropping 25% of your
 unbanked coins on the ground for anyone to grab
 7% MYSTERY BOX - a wobbling box; touch it for a random buff
 (2x coins for 20s, super speed, ghost mode, magnet)
 3% JACKPOT - the door explodes into a fountain of 200+ coins with a
 loud siren and a screen-wide golden flash. Everyone on
 the server hears it and sees a marker on that door.

=== THE CONTENTION MECHANIC (this is what makes it multiplayer) ===
- HOT DOORS: after any door pays out well, it glows red-hot and its PAYOUT
 odds double for 15 seconds. A floating flame icon marks it server-wide.
 Players will sprint across the map and fight over these. This single rule
 generates all the rivalry - do not cut it.
- Doors go on an 8-second cooldown per player after ringing, but ANY other
 player can ring the same door immediately. First to reach it wins the roll.
- DROPPED COINS ARE PUBLIC. When someone gets trapped or caught, their spilled
 coins are free for anyone. Vultures are a valid playstyle.
- Residents chase the player who rang, but will switch targets if another
 player runs closer to them. Players can and will bait residents into rivals.
- No direct player combat. No weapons. All conflict is positional and comedic.

=== ROUND STRUCTURE ===
Server size: 12 players.

INTERMISSION (30 seconds)
 Players stand in the cul-de-sac. Big flip-clock countdown on the mailbox.
 Upgrade truck is open. Round leaderboard from the previous round is displayed
 on a billboard. Winner of the last round wears a glowing crown.

ROUND (3 minutes)
 House unlocks. All 50 doors go live. Coins are worth 1x for the first minute,
 1.5x in the second, 2x in the final minute - so the last 60 seconds are a
 frantic, greedy scramble where nobody wants to leave to bank.

 Final 10 seconds: "LAST CALL" siren. Any unbanked coins at the buzzer are
 LOST. Watching players sprint for the mailbox is the best moment in the game.

RESULTS (15 seconds)
 Top 3 podium rises out of the lawn. Confetti. XP awarded.

=== LEVEL-UP SYSTEM ===
Persistent account level 1-60. XP = total coins banked, all-time.
Leveling is fast early (level 5 in the first two rounds) and slows gradually.

Each level grants 1 upgrade point. Five upgrade tracks, 12 ranks each,
purchased from the ICE CREAM TRUCK parked in the cul-de-sac:

 LUCK Shifts the outcome table. At max rank: PAYOUT 60%, RESIDENT 8%,
 TRAP 4%, JACKPOT 8%. Never removes risk entirely.
 SPRINT Move speed +2% per rank. Also increases sprint stamina.
 NERVE Reduces trap stun duration and lets you shrug off the first
 resident hit each round.
 POCKETS Increases unbanked coin cap. Low ranks force frequent banking
 trips; high ranks let you gamble huge stacks.
 REACH Ring doorbells from further away, and ring 15% faster per rank.

Show a chunky, sticker-styled upgrade menu with big plus buttons and a
satisfying "ka-chunk" sound on purchase.

MILESTONE UNLOCKS (cosmetic, drives long-term retention):
 Lvl 5 Bathrobe outfit
 Lvl 10 Bicycle (faster, but you can't carry coins while riding)
 Lvl 15 Custom doorbell chime (you choose the sound everyone hears)
 Lvl 25 Glowing footprint trail
 Lvl 40 Pizza delivery uniform - residents hesitate for 1 second
 Lvl 60 Golden thumb - permanent visible aura, a flex

=== LEADERBOARDS ===
1. LIVE ROUND BOARD - right side of screen, always visible, top 5 by banked
 coins this round. Your own row is pinned at the bottom if you're not top 5.
2. THE BILLBOARD - a physical billboard in the cul-de-sac, three tabs:
 - WEEKLY: most coins banked, resets Monday. Top 3 get a crown cosmetic.
 - ALL-TIME DOORBELLS RUNG: a pure volume stat. Absurd numbers. Very sticky.
 - RESIDENTS OUTRUN: bragging-rights stat for chase survivors.
3. Persistent Roblox leaderstats: Level, Banked (all-time), Rung.

=== THE HOUSE - VISUAL DESIGN ===
Setting: a suburban cul-de-sac frozen at golden-hour dusk. Warm orange light,
long purple shadows, a few fireflies, sprinklers hissing on the lawns.

The house is the star and should read as WRONG on first sight: a single
suburban home that has been vertically stacked five stories tall, each floor a
mismatched architectural style - vinyl siding, then brick, then a log cabin,
then stucco, then a slightly-too-formal Victorian top floor with a widow's
walk. It leans very slightly. It is far too tall for its plot.

Its entire front face is a collage of 50 DOORS crammed edge to edge with no
logic - doors at floor level, doors halfway up the wall, doors upside down,
doors behind other doors. Players reach upper doors via exterior wooden
staircases, a fire escape, scaffolding, a trellis, and one very long ladder.

DOOR VARIETY (each door type visually telegraphs its personality):
 screen door, castle drawbridge, refrigerator door, cat flap, bank vault,
 airlock, submarine hatch, saloon swinging doors, revolving door, elevator
 doors, a beaded curtain, a door made entirely of cardboard, one door that
 is clearly just a painting of a door, a doggy door only small avatars fit
 through, a door with 40 locks on it, a door labeled DO NOT.

Art direction: chunky low-poly, heavy saturation, no realism. Palette is mint
green, salmon, mustard yellow, and dusty teal. Everything slightly oversized
and rounded - mailbox is comically huge, the doorbells are the size of dinner
plates. Cartoon squash-and-stretch on every interaction.

VFX: expanding white sound-rings pulse out of a rung doorbell. Coins are fat
spinning discs with a chime. Traps are silent-film slapstick - pies, anvils,
paint buckets, a single enormous boxing glove on a spring.

RESIDENT NPCS: rotund, furious, wearing bathrobes and curlers, wielding
slippers, rolled newspapers, and one with a garden hose. They run with an
exaggerated waddle. They shout muffled gibberish, never real words. When they
give up, they stop, shake a fist, and slam the door.

AUDIO: 50 distinct doorbell chimes - normal ding-dongs, a foghorn, a cow, a
full 8-second orchestral fanfare, one that's just a man saying "hello."
Background: cicadas, distant lawnmower, an ice cream truck jingle looping
faintly. The jackpot siren should be genuinely startling.

UI: thick rounded borders, hand-drawn sticker aesthetic, bouncy tweened
animations on every number change. Coin counter should physically jiggle.

=== MOBILE ===
Design for mobile first. Single large contextual RING button bottom-right,
sprint on the left thumbstick double-tap. Never require more than one finger.

=== MONETIZATION (keep it light) ===
Cosmetic-only outfits and doorbell chimes. One 2x-coins gamepass. A "Skip the
Walk" teleport-to-mailbox consumable. Do not sell Luck.

=== SUCCESS CRITERIA ===
A brand-new player should ring their first doorbell within 8 seconds of
spawning and understand the entire game without reading a word of tutorial.

answers.ask: Do any of the fifty doors open into a real interior a player can walk into, or are they all shallow reveals on the facade?
answers.answer: All fifty are shallow facade reveals only; doors react with their outcome but do not lead into walkable interiors.

answers.ask: How wide should the cul-de-sac be? Twelve players sprinting between the house and the mailbox needs the run to feel costly but not slow.
answers.answer: Keep it compact: place the mailbox roughly 80 studs from the house's main door cluster, with the cul-de-sac about 140 studs across. Banking should take a short committed sprint, not a long traversal.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] free — Q: Do any of the fifty doors open into a real interior a player can walk into, or are they all shallow reveals on the facade? A: All fifty are shallow facade reveals only; doors react with their outcome but do not lead into walkable interiors.
- [author] scale — Q: How wide should the cul-de-sac be? Twelve players sprinting between the house and the mailbox needs the run to feel costly but not slow. A: Keep it compact: place the mailbox roughly 80 studs from the house's main door cluster, with the cul-de-sac about 140 studs across. Banking should take a short committed sprint, not a long traversal.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a compact suburban cul-de-sac about 140 studs across at golden-hour dusk. Make one absurd five-story house the focal build: five stacked mismatched levels of vinyl siding, brick, log cabin, stucco, and formal Victorian architecture with a widow's walk, all leaning slightly. Crowd its front facade with exactly 50 shallow non-enterable door reveals, including screen, drawbridge, refrigerator, cat-flap, vault, airlock, hatch, saloon, revolving, elevator, beaded-curtain, cardboard, painted, doggy, forty-lock, and “DO NOT” variants. Reach upper doors by exterior wooden stairs, a fire escape, scaffolding, a trellis, and one long ladder. Place a comically huge mailbox roughly 80 studs from the main door cluster, an ice-cream upgrade truck, physical leaderboard billboard, and rising top-three lawn podium around the cul-de-sac. Use chunky rounded low-poly forms, oversized dinner-plate doorbells, mint green, salmon, mustard yellow, and dusty teal, with warm orange light, purple shadows, fireflies, lawns, and sprinklers.

## Genre
Party & Casual is dominant, with Simulation secondary for the repeatable door-and-banking loop and persistent upgrades.

## Shape and preset
Use `arena-stacked`, Multi-Level Arena, from outside Party & Casual's usual set because five playable exterior levels overhang the lawn and each other. Preset: none; the round remains in one continuous cul-de-sac and does not match a lobby-isolated minigame stage.

## Config requirements
Use `landmark-focal` for the impossible five-story house, `path-circulation` for routes among doors, mailbox, truck, billboard, and podium, and `social-hub` for the intermission cul-de-sac. Use `trigger-task` for 50 visible doorbell stations and the mailbox bank station, `physics-rig` for slapstick pie, anvil, paint-bucket, and spring-glove outcomes, `tracker-leaderboard` for the physical billboard, and `spawn-first-reveal` for a joining view facing the house.

## Layout requirements
For `trigger-task`, place one ring trigger at each of 50 doorbells and one deposit trigger at the mailbox 80 studs away. Use `collectible-nodes` for coins emitted in front of payout doors and dropped publicly at trap or chase locations. Use `powerup-buffs` for mystery-box pickups. Use `spawner-npc` at the shallow door reveals for resident entrances. For `spawn-first-reveal`, place 12 cul-de-sac start slots facing the house and within an eight-second run of a door.

## Layout components
One 140-stud cul-de-sac contains the five-story, 50-door house, 80-stud house-to-mailbox banking run, lawns, upgrade truck, billboard, and lawn podium. Exterior stairs, fire escape, scaffolding, trellis, and ladder connect all facade levels. Every door is a shallow reveal; there are no interiors. Streets and property edges bound play. Keep the banking route unobstructed and the full facade readable in frame.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: the five stacked facade levels and their exterior access routes must be authoritative because a top-down image would hide most doors.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is medium, fixed by the 140-stud cul-de-sac and legibility of 50 doorbells. The theme is saturated low-poly suburban slapstick at golden hour. Use `P2` because five exterior levels, stairs, scaffolding, and doors overhang lower play; do not use `P3` because all doors are confirmed shallow facade reveals.
